errorReport.subject: Error report
errorReport.body:
Hello,

The app encountered an error. The attached file contains technical information about your phone (model, system, rounded memory and free space) and how the app ran, without your card, your CAN or your vote. This message and your address are deleted after processing.

Thank you for your help.

Référendum Citoyen app, v{{version}} (build {{build}})
errorReport.expiredTitle: This report is no longer available
errorReport.expiredBody: Your vote has just been recorded, and the vote lines were removed from the log so that this report cannot be tied to your ballot. The report prepared before that removal can therefore no longer be sent. Tap the report button again to create a new one.
errorReport.consentBody: This report contains technical information about your phone and how the app ran, without your card, your CAN or your vote. The message is deleted after processing.
errorReport.consentBetaAttachment: Test version: an attachment also contains this test's vote proof, not anonymised, for the technical team.
errorReport.fallbackMessage: The app encountered an unexpected problem. You can send a report to help us fix it.
errorReport.successButton: Send this vote's logs to the team
errorReport.successBody:
Hello,

This TEST vote succeeded. The attachments hold the session logs and, as JSON, the vote proof (query proof), its public signals, the selector and the registration parameters — NOT anonymised, for the test programme's technical team only.

Thank you for your help.

— Référendum Citoyen app, v{{version}} (build {{build}})

welcome.title: Welcome!
welcome.text: We are building an app that lets French citizens collectively express their political will through verifiable citizen referendums. When a large number of citizens take part in an authenticated vote, the result becomes a strong democratic expression, publicly verifiable, and politically hard to ignore.

accordions.title: How is this different from a poll?
accordions.content: A poll surveys a small sample of people to estimate an opinion. These verified citizen referendums let every citizen actually vote, only once, anonymously and verifiably. A poll gives an estimate. A citizen referendum gives a real result that everyone can check and that is politically hard to ignore.

accordions.title: How is this different from a petition?
accordions.content: A petition expresses declarative support, without guaranteeing that each signer is a French adult citizen or that the same person only signs once, and it relies on a list controlled by its organisers, who set the wording and publish the result themselves. By contrast, this verified citizen referendum relies on ID-card authentication that guarantees 1 person = 1 vote, lets you vote for, against or blank, and makes the result verifiable by anyone via a public registry independent of the organisers. Where a petition measures a mobilisation aimed at a position, this mechanism enables a neutral and verifiable expression of an authenticated collective decision by citizens, giving it a democratic and political weight of an entirely different nature.

accordions.title: Is this an official referendum?
accordions.content: No. It is a verified citizen referendum. Every voter can verify that their vote has been counted in the public online registry. But a referendum in which hundreds of thousands or millions of authenticated citizens take part becomes a major democratic fact.

sections.title: A unique and publicly verifiable vote
sections.intro:
The right to vote is verified by reading the chip on your ID document directly on your phone. This check guarantees:
1. that you are French and an adult
2. that the same person can only vote once

This check is performed locally on your phone: no central identity file is created.

accordions.title: What do I need to vote?
accordions.content: You need your French national ID card in credit-card format, still valid, and a smartphone with NFC reading and the Référendum Citoyen app installed.

accordions.title: Which ID card?
accordions.content: The national ID card in credit-card format, issued since August 2021, read with its CAN code (six digits on the front). It holds a chip your phone reads directly, with no central file. The older laminated card and the passport are not accepted in this version: the new card is requested at the town hall and its renewal is free.

accordions.title: Why not use FranceConnect?
accordions.content: Because FranceConnect relies on a central identity file. Our system relies instead on a local check of the ID document with no central database linking identity and vote. FranceConnect is managed by the State; our system is independent of the government.

accordions.title: Can someone vote twice using two phones?
accordions.content: No. The identity proof prevents duplicate voting rights.

accordions.title: Is there a possibility of double voting?
accordions.content:
The system prevents the same person from voting twice with the same ID document.

Under the current rollout of the new electronic ID documents, a person who reports their card lost and obtains a new one could in theory vote twice. This case remains extremely rare today. In the long run we can make this risk disappear technically: once lost and reissued ID documents share a common identifier preventing any double use.

accordions.title: Going further
accordions.content:
Technical code link: https://github.com/rarimo/rarime-rn-sdk

Rarimo's project with existing votes: https://freedomtool.org/

sections.title: Registering your card
sections.intro: Enter the CAN code, the six digits printed on the front of your card, bottom right. It only opens the chip. It is never sent over the internet and never saved in the app. Lay the card against the back of the phone, without moving, case removed.

sections.title: One card per person
sections.intro: You vote with your ID card, and a card votes once per question, whichever phone it is on. One person, one vote.

sections.title: Your key
sections.intro: After registering, back up your key. Without it, a reinstall stops you from voting.

sections.title: Your data
sections.intro: Your name, date of birth and nationality are read on your phone to check your eligibility. Nothing links your vote to your identity. No identity data is kept after the vote.

sections.title: A guaranteed-anonymous vote
sections.intro:
We prove that you have the right to vote, not who you are. Your identity is checked only to confirm your right to vote. Then your identity is separated from your vote before it is sent. The vote sent to the tamper-proof, publicly visible registry contains no information that could link your identity to your vote. As a result, the counted ballot cannot be traced back to an ID document.

In technical terms, voting happens inside a smart contract on a chain (Rarimo's to begin with).

accordions.title: How do you guarantee "1 person = 1 vote" without knowing the identity?
accordions.content: The ID document is read directly on the phone to verify that the person is French, an adult, and is exercising their right to vote only once. A cryptographic token proving the right to vote is then generated. This proof confirms that the person is entitled to vote without revealing their identity. No central file links identity to vote. The system lets you vote but does not know who you are.

accordions.title: Who can see my vote?
accordions.content: Nobody. Your vote is anonymised before being sent.

accordions.title: Can the State know what I voted for?
accordions.content: No. No central file links identity and vote. If an ID document is used after your vote, the system detects that it has already been used and prevents a second vote. Among the options when you cast a vote, an "I refuse to vote" option exists to publicly signal that no vote has been expressed with your ID document. This protects you.

sections.title: A transparent vote
sections.intro:
Every vote receives a unique identifier publicly visible in the ballot's registry. This means:
– every citizen can verify that their vote has been counted and matches their choice
– anyone can verify the total number of votes

accordions.title: Can I check that my vote has been counted?
accordions.content: Yes. Your vote has a unique identifier visible to everyone in the registry. This identifier lets every citizen check that their vote is recorded and counted in the total. Anyone can verify the result.

accordions.title: Can I check other people's votes?
accordions.content: Yes. The total number of votes is public and verifiable. Results are visible in real time as they progress.

sections.title: Others can vote on your phone
sections.intro: Several people can vote from the same phone. Each vote requires reading a different ID document. After the vote, the phone keeps neither your name, nor your date of birth, nor the contents of the chip. It keeps your voting key, which says nothing about who you are and which lets you vote again later with the same document. That key never leaves the phone: what is sent is a mathematical proof, not your data.

accordions.title: Can the phone's owner see my vote?
accordions.content: No. The vote is wiped from the phone after sending. The phone works like a polling station, not like a ballot.

accordions.title: Can you vote on behalf of someone else?
accordions.content: No. The ID document is required. Using someone else's ID document is identity fraud and is a criminal offence.

sections.title: A registry distributed across many computers and publicly verifiable
sections.intro: Votes are not stored on a single server. They are recorded in a registry distributed across many computers and public. This means that no single actor can change or remove the results without it being visible. The system relies on public verification of results rather than trust in a central authority.

accordions.title: Can a third party shut down the app?
accordions.content: Even if the app disappears, the votes remain recorded in the openly distributed file, accessible independently of the app. The ballot cannot be interrupted during the voting period.

accordions.title: Can a third party delete the results?
accordions.content: No. They are stored in an electronic ballot box accessible to everyone.

accordions.title: Can the results be rigged?
accordions.content: The system is not based on trusting a central server, but on public verification of the results. The right to vote is verified locally on the phone, the vote is anonymised before being sent, then recorded in a public registry that anyone can consult. Any attempt to alter the result would be immediately visible, since anyone can check the number of votes recorded.

accordions.title: What happens if a flaw is discovered?
accordions.content: The system relies on transparency rather than secrecy. The code is open source, so independent experts can review it at any time. If a flaw is identified, it can be fixed by the team behind the app publicly and quickly. This permanent-audit logic reinforces the security of the system rather than weakening it.

contribuer.title: Contribute
contribuer.text: Référendum Citoyen is a citizens' movement. There is no state and no party behind it: a small team, and you. Voting is free for you, but every vote costs a few cents to record on the chain, and the app has to be built and maintained. Your donations are what let others vote. Donations happen on our website, never in the app, and nothing links them to your vote.

petitions.title: Open petitions
petitions.text: A petition is a question you support with your e-mail address, with no app and no ID document. When a petition reaches 500,000 supporters, it becomes a citizens' referendum in this app. And tomorrow, a national referendum: that is what the main question asks, which the president elected in 2027 will have to implement. Seven questions are open for petition on our website.
petitions.entryText: Seven questions are open for petition on our website. A petition that reaches 500,000 supporters becomes a citizens' referendum here.

newsletter.text: Leave us your e-mail to follow the results and the next questions. On our website, never in the app: your address is not linked to any vote.
